svg.aria-label: What a buyer actually owns when a parking space is allotted with a flat
svg.text: What you own when you are “given” parking
Three arrangements, sold in almost identical language, with very different consequences

g.text: Named in the agreement, with the bay number
The specific space is identified in the registered agreement for sale. This is the version worth insisting on.
Allotted by letter, after the agreement
An allotment letter is a promise from the builder, not a right recorded against the flat. It can be revisited at handover.
You have access to the basement, not to a place in it. Fine at 40 per cent occupancy, contested at 95.

svg.text: Common areas belong to the society, not the builder, once conveyance happens
Which is why a builder selling stilt or open parking as a separate saleable unit has repeatedly been struck down. Get the position in writing.
